data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Ides' which means 'to split' or 'to divide'. The suffix '-son' denotes 'son'. In Roman mythology, the Ides of March was a significant religious day, celebrated in the honor of the god Jupiter. This name is therefore a tribute to the ancient Roman tradition and the power and wisdom of Jupiter.

At the same time, it holds significance in Roman culture as a term associated with the Ides of March - a crucial and revered day in the Roman calendar. As such, the name can serve as a conversation starter or an interesting topic for exploration, providing opportunities to delve into the fascinating history of both Greece and Rome.

Jupiter was revered for his protective and all-knowing nature, as well as his role as supreme deity. By adopting the name "Idelson," one may be symbolslically embracing the wisdom and strength that Jupiter represents. In many ways, the name can serve as a daily reminder to strive for wisdom, to seek understanding, and to approach life with a strong and unyielding spirit.
